BIOET 501: This course explores a variety of theories and methods in bioethics and applies them to a selection of current topics.
BIOET 502: This course explores systemic and structural issues in bioethics, and the theories and methodologies required to address them.
BIOET 504: This course will examine the complex ways ethical issues are a component of research in science and engineering.
BIOET 531: This course provides a close examination into the field of neuroethics and the responsible application of advances in neuroscience research and neuroengineering.
BIOET 533: BIOET 533 will provide students with an understanding of the ethical dimensions of renewable energy and sustainability systems and with skills to analyze related case studies.
BIOET 540: This course will examine in a bioethical context a variety of ways relations of power and values intersect.
BIOET 590: Continuing seminars in bioethics that consist of a series of individual presentations by faculty, students, or outside speakers.
BIOET 594: Supervised student activities on research projects identified on an individual or small-group basis.
BIOET 595: Supervised off-campus, nongroup instruction, including field experiences, practicums, or internships related to bioethics.
BIOET 596: Creative projects, including nonthesis research, that are supervised on an individual basis and which fall outside the scope of formal courses.
BIOET 597: Formal courses given infrequently to explore a topic or topics in bioethics in depth.
BIOET 602: Students will teach lower-level undergraduate courses in bioethics, including courses on the undergraduate minor in bioethics and medical humanities.
